paragraphs: All references to "LSB Industries," "LSB," the "Company," "we," "us," and "our" refer to LSB Industries, Inc. and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, except where the context makes clear that the reference is only to LSB Industries, Inc. itself and not its subsidiaries. Notes referenced throughout this document refer to consolidated financial statement footnote disclosures that are found in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this report. Capitalized terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed thereto under the heading "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements – Defined Terms."

LSB is a Delaware corporation, formed in 1968, and headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. LSB is committed to playing a leadership role in the production of low and no carbon products that build, feed and power the world. We seek to accomplish this goal through the manufacture and marketing of essential products for the agricultural and industrial markets, and in the future, low and no carbon products, all with an emphasis on a culture of excellence in customer experience. The Company manufactures ammonia and ammonia-related products in El Dorado, Arkansas (the "El Dorado Facility"), Cherokee, Alabama (the "Cherokee Facility"), and Pryor, Oklahoma (the "Pryor Facility"), and operates a facility on behalf of Covestro LLC ("Covestro") in Baytown, Texas (the "Baytown Facility"). Our products are sold through distributors and directly to end customers, such as farmers, ranchers, and fertilizer dealers, throughout the United States and parts of Canada, and to explosives manufacturers in the United States and other parts of North America.
Our business manufactures products for two principal markets: (a) Industrial and (b) Agricultural. The chart below highlights representative products and applications in each of our end markets.

The products we manufacture at our facilities are primarily derived from natural gas (a raw material). Our facilities and production processes have been designed to produce products that are marketable at nearly each stage of production. This design has allowed us to develop and deploy a business model optimizing the mix of products to capture the value opportunities in the end markets we serve with a focus on balancing our production.

For additional information regarding our net sales, operating results and total assets for the past three fiscal years, see the Consolidated Financial Statements included in this report.

We aim to be a leader in the production of low and no carbon products that build, feed and power the world. We plan to accomplish this goal by leveraging our existing business platform and portfolio of assets to produce low carbon products, utilizing our significant manufacturing expertise and experience in ammonia and hydrogen plant operations, optimizing our liquidity and free cash flows to generate growth, and creating a network of partners that bring additional knowledge, expertise and relationships.

With respect to our current portfolio of products, we pursue a strategy of balancing the sale of product as fertilizer into the agriculture markets at spot prices or short duration pre-sales and developing and maintaining industrial customers that purchase substantial quantities of products, primarily under contractual obligations and/or pricing arrangements that generally provide for the pass through of some raw material and other manufacturing costs. We believe this product and market diversification strategy allows us to have more consistent levels of production compared to some of our competitors and helps reduce the volatility risk inherent in the prices of our raw material and/or the changes in demand for our products.

The strategy of developing and maintaining industrial customers helps to moderate the risk inherent in the agricultural markets where spot sales prices of our agricultural products may not have a correlation to natural gas raw material costs but rather reflect market conditions for like and competing nitrogen sources. This volatility of sales pricing in our agricultural products may, from time to time, compromise our ability to recover our full cost to produce the product. Industrial customers assume the volatility risk associated with the raw material costs and mitigate the effects of seasonality in the agricultural sector. Additionally, the lack of sufficient non-seasonal agricultural sales volume to operate our manufacturing facilities at optimum levels can preclude us from balancing production and storage capabilities. Looking forward, we remain focused on upgrading margins by maximizing downstream production.

Our strategy also includes evaluating further investments in low carbon opportunities, potential acquisitions of strategic assets or companies, joint ventures with other companies and investments in additional production capacity where we believe those acquisitions, joint ventures or expansion of production capacity will enhance the value of the Company and provide appropriate returns.

As discussed in more detail under "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations–Key Operating Initiatives," we believe our future results of operations and financial condition will depend significantly on our ability to successfully implement the following key initiatives:
• Invest to Improve Environmental, Health & Safety at our Facilities;
• Improve the Reliability at our Facilities while Supplying our Customers with Products of the Highest Quality;

paragraphs: Our sales and profits are heavily affected by the costs and availability of primary raw materials. These primary raw materials are typically subject to considerable price volatility, and recent global supply chain disruptions and increased inflation in the United States have led to further heightened volatility. Historically, when there have been rapid increases in the cost of these primary raw materials, we have sometimes been unable to timely increase our sales prices to cover all of the higher costs incurred. While we periodically enter into futures/forward contracts to economically hedge against price increases in certain of these raw materials, we may not effectively manage against price fluctuations in those raw materials.

Natural gas represents the primary raw material in the production of most of our chemical products. Although we enter into contracts with certain customers that provide for the pass-through of raw material costs, we have a substantial amount of sales that do not provide for the pass-through of raw material costs. Also, the spot sales prices of our agricultural products may not correlate to the cost of natural gas but rather reflect market conditions for similar and competing nitrogen sources. This lack of correlation can compromise our ability to recover our full cost to produce the products in this market. As a result, in the future, we may not be able to pass along to all of our customers the full amount of any increases in raw material costs. Future price fluctuations in our raw materials may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations.

Additionally, we depend on certain vendors to deliver natural gas and other key components that are required in the production of our products. Any disruption in the supply of natural gas and other key components could result in lost production or delayed shipments.

The price of natural gas in North America is volatile and impacted by geopolitical instability, the level of domestic drilling activity and temporary supply disruption from severe weather events. In addition, future production of natural gas from shale formations could be reduced by regulatory changes that restrict drilling or hydraulic fracturing or increase its cost or by reduction in oil exploration and development prompted by lower oil prices and resulting in production of less associated natural gas. Further, increased demand for natural gas, particularly in the Gulf Coast Region, due to increased industrial demand, increased power generation demand, especially from artificial intelligence data centers, and increased natural gas exports could result in increased natural gas prices.

We have suspended in the past, and could suspend in the future, production at our chemical facilities due to, among other things, the high cost or lack of availability of natural gas and other key components, which could adversely affect our competitiveness in the markets we serve. Accordingly, our business, financial condition, liquidity and results of operations could be materially affected in the future by the lack of availability of natural gas and other key components and increase costs relating to the purchase of natural gas and other key components.

We manufacture products at four facilities. Operational disruptions could occur for many reasons, including natural disaster, weather, unplanned maintenance and other manufacturing problems, disease, strikes or other labor unrest or transportation interruptions. Extreme weather events, including temperature extremes, depending on the severity and location, have the potential not only to damage our facilities and disrupt our operations, but also to affect adversely the distribution of our products. Moreover, our facilities may be subject to failure of equipment that may be difficult to replace or have long delivery lead times, due in part to a limited number of suppliers and could result in operational disruptions. The suspension of operations at any of these facilities, or significant impacts on any of their operations as a result of supply chain disruption, could adversely affect our ability to produce our products and fulfill our commitments and could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial condition, results of operations and business.

paragraphs: In May 2024, we announced an agreement to supply, for a five-year period commencing January 1, 2025, up to 150,000 short tons per year of low carbon ammonium nitrate solution ("ANS") to Freeport Minerals Corporation ("Freeport"). In early 2025 we began supplying conventional ANS to Freeport from our El Dorado Facility, and expect to phase in the low carbon contracted volume in late 2026. Freeport intends to use the low carbon ANS purchased from us for its United States copper mining operations.

In April 2022, we entered into an agreement with Lapis Carbon Solutions ("Lapis") to develop a project to capture and sequester CO2 at our El Dorado Facility. Lapis, backed by Cresta Fund Management, a Dallas-based middle-market infrastructure investment firm, will invest the majority of the capital required for project development. The project is expected to be completed and operational by the end of 2026, subject to the approval of a Class VI permit, at which time CO2 injections are expected to begin. Once operational, the project at the El Dorado site will initially capture and sequester approximately 400,000 to 500,000 metric tons of CO2 per year in underground saline aquifers.

The sequestered CO2 generated from the facility's ammonia production is expected to qualify for federal tax credits under Internal Revenue Code Section 45Q, which are $85 per metric ton of CO2 captured and sequestered. Lapis, as the majority owner of the carbon capture and sequestration equipment, will earn the 45Q tax credits and will pay us a fee for each ton of CO2 captured and sequestered, which we expect to commence at the end of 2026. Once in operation, the sequestered CO2 is expected to reduce our overall scope 1 GHG emissions by approximately 25% from current levels. In addition, sequestering approximately 400,000 to 500,000 metric tons of CO2 annually is expected to enable us to produce approximately 305,000 to 380,000 metric tons of low carbon ammonia annually, a product that could potentially be sold at higher price levels than conventional ammonia. In February 2023, a key milestone was achieved in the advancement of our low carbon ammonia project at El Dorado by filing a pre-construction Class VI permit application with the United States Environmental Protection Agency (the "EPA"). The EPA recognized the application as complete in March 2023 and is currently in the review process. In June 2025, Lapis completed the drilling of a stratigraphic injection well at the El Dorado site and has been gathering data to support the EPA in its continuing technical review of our Class VI application. Lapis resubmitted the pre-construction Class VI permit application to the EPA in December 2025. Once the project receives EPA approval, we intend to use this well for CO2 injections.

Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" 之合併財務報表腳註揭露。未於 herein 定義之專有名詞，其含義應依 "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements – Defined Terms" 之標題所定義。

LSB 為設立於德克薩斯州奧克拉荷馬市之奧克拉荷馬州公司，成立於 1968 年。LSB 承諾在生產低碳及零碳產品方面扮演領導角色，以建設、飼養及供應世界。我們透過製造與行銷農業與工業市場之必要產品，以及未來之低碳及零碳產品，來達成此目標，並強調以卓越之客戶體驗文化為重點。本公司於阿肯色州艾爾多羅 ("El Dorado Facility"), 阿拉巴馬州切羅基 ("Cherokee Facility"), 奧克拉荷馬州普賴爾 ("Pryor Facility") 製造氨與氨相關產品，並為 Covestro LLC ("Covestro") 在德克薩斯州巴頓 ("Baytown Facility") 設有廠區。我們之產品透過經銷商直接銷售至終端客戶，如農民、牧場主及肥料經銷商，遍及美國與加拿大部分地區，並銷售至美國及其他北美地區之炸藥製造商。
本公司業務製造產品用於兩個主要市場：(a) 工業與 (b) 農業。下圖顯示我們各終端市場之代表性產品與應用。
我們於廠區製造之產品主要來自天然氣（原料）。廠區與生產流程已設計為在生產過程之幾乎每個階段均可銷售產品。此設計使我們得以發展並部署一種商業模式，以最佳化產品組合，以捕捉我們服務之終端市場之價值機會，並著重於平衡生產。
下表總結與我們產品相關之淨銷售額資訊：2025 2024
合併淨銷售額百分比：AN & 硝酸 鎂胺硝酸鹽 (UAN) 氨
如需有關我們過去三個會計年度之淨銷售額、營運結果及總資產之額外資訊，請參閱本報告所包含之合併財務報表。
我們旨在成為生產低碳及零碳產品之領導者，以建設、飼養及供應世界。我們計畫透過運用現有業務平台與資產組合，生產低碳產品，利用我們在氨與氫氣廠運作方面之重大製造專業知識與經驗，優化流動性與自由現金流以產生成長，並建立一個帶有額外知識、專業與關係之合作夥伴網路來達成此目標。
就我們目前的產品組合而言，我們採行一種策略，即在農業市場以現貨價格或短暫期預售方式銷售產品作為肥料，同時開發並維持工業客戶，這些客戶購買大量產品，主要透過契約義務及/或價格安排，通常會將部分原材料及其他製造成本轉嫁給客戶。我們認為，這種產品與市場多元化策略，使我們的生產水平較一些競爭對手更為穩定，並有助於降低原材料價格或產品需求變動所內含的波動風險。

開發並維持工業客戶的策略，有助於緩和農業市場內在的風險，其中我們農業產品的現貨銷售價格可能與天然氣原材料成本無關，而是反映類似及競爭性氮肥來源的市場條件。我們農業產品銷售價格的波動性，有時可能影響我們回收產品完整成本的能力。工業客戶承擔與原材料成本相關的波動風險，並緩解農業部門的季節性影響。此外，若非季節性農業銷售體積不足，無法讓我們的製造設施以最佳水平運作，可能會阻礙我們平衡生產與儲存能力。展望未來，我們持續專注於透過最大化下游生產來提升毛利率。
我們的策略也包括評估進一步投資低碳機會、潛在收購戰略資產或公司、與其他公司成立合資企業，以及投資額外的生產能力，我們認為這些收購、合資企業或擴充生產能力將能提升本公司價值並提供適當回報。
如在「項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析–關鍵營運重點」中更詳細討論，我們認為未來營運成果與財務狀況將大幅取決於我們成功執行以下關鍵重點的能耐：
• 投資改善設施的環境、健康與安全；
• 在供應客戶高品質產品的同時，提升設施的可靠性；

paragraphs: 2024年5月，本公司宣佈與Freeport Minerals Corporation（"Freeport"）簽訂協議，自2025年1月1日起，於五年期間每年供應最高達150,000短噸的低碳氨硝酸溶液（"ANS"）。2025年初，本公司已開始從El Dorado廠區供應傳統ANS至Freeport，預計於2026年底逐步增加低碳合約供應量。Freeport預計將從本公司購入的低碳ANS用於其美國銅礦開採作業。

2022年4月，本公司與Lapis Carbon Solutions（"Lapis"）簽訂協議，開發於El Dorado廠區進行二氧化碳捕獲與封存（CCS）的專案。Lapis由位於達拉斯的中型基礎設施投資公司Cresta Fund Management支持，將投資專案開發所需資金的絕大多數。該專案預計於2026年底完成並投入運作，前提是取得Class VI許可證的批准，屆時預計開始進行二氧化碳注入。專案投入運作後，El Dorado廠區將初期每年捕獲與封存約400,000至500,000公噸的二氧化碳於地下鹹水層。

來自廠區氨生產所產生的封存二氧化碳，預計符合美國內政部稅收碼第45Q條款所規定的聯邦稅 credits，每公噸二氧化碳捕獲與封存可獲得85美元的稅 credits。作為碳捕獲與封存設備的大多數所有者，Lapis將獲得45Q稅 credits，並為每公噸捕獲與封存的二氧化碳支付我們費用，預計於2026年底開始。專案投入運作後，封存的二氧化碳預計將使本公司總體範疇1 GHG排放量較目前水平減少約25%。此外，每年封存約400,000至500,000公噸二氧化碳，預計將使本公司每年生產約305,000至380,000公噸的低碳氨，一種可能以高於傳統氨價格銷售的產品。2023年2月，在El Dorado廠區的低碳氨專案進展中，達成關鍵里程碑，即向美國環境保護署（"EPA"）提交預建Class VI許可證申請。EPA於2023年3月認可申請為完整，目前正進行審查。2025年6月，Lapis在El Dorado廠區完成地層注入井的鑽探，並正在收集數據以支持EPA對我們Class VI申請的持續技術審查。Lapis於2025年12月重新提交預建Class VI許可證申請至EPA。專案取得EPA批准後，本公司預計將使用此井進行二氧化碳注入。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
成本及原物料供應不足可能對我們的獲利造成重大影響。
我們依賴有限數量的關鍵設施。
我們的化學製造設施年齡較大，會增加非預期停機的風險，該風險可能相當重大。
我們的營運及產品的生產與處理過程涉及重大風險與危害。
我們的運輸與配送活動依賴第三方服務提供者，這使我們面臨超出我們控制範圍的風險與不確定性，可能對我們的營運造成不利影響。
我們可能無法在合適或經濟的方式下，或甚至完全無法成功開發與實施我們的低碳氨專案。
我們所服務的市場競爭激烈。
季節性因素可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司銷售收入的相當大一部分依賴於有限數量的客戶。
本公司業務面臨與衍生性商品相關的風險，以及本公司避險活動可能無法有效進行的風險。
網路安全風險可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司可能進行某些戰略交易，這些交易可能對本公司財務狀況造成不利影響。
與本公司產業及市場相關的風險
進口氮基產品增加可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
惡劣天氣條件及氣候變遷可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
與我們流動性及負債相關的風險
我們可能無法產生足夠的現金來償還我們的負債，並可能需要採取其他行動以履行我們負債協議下的義務，這些行動可能不會成功。
我們目前的負債水平可能會限制我們的財務及營運活動，並對我們產生額外負債以資助未來需求的能力產生不利影響。
儘管我們目前的負債水平，我們仍可能產生更多負債，其優先順位與現有義務相同或更高，包括有擔保負債，這將增加 herein 所描述的風險。
與法律、法規及合規事項相關的風險
目前及未來影響我們業務的立法或法規要求，可能會導致成本增加、收入減少、現金流及流動性下降，或對我們業務產生其他負面影響。
我們可能沒有足夠的保險。
我們可能需要修改或擴充我們的營運、銷售及報告程序，並安裝額外設備，以符合目前及可能的未來政府法規。
paragraphs: 本公司銷售與獲利受主要原物料成本與可得性影響甚鉅。這些主要原物料通常價格波動幅度相當大，近期全球供應鏈中斷與美國通貨膨脹增加，導致波動更加劇烈。歷史上，當這些主要原物料成本快速上升時，本公司偶爾無法及時提高銷售價格以彌補所有增加的成本。雖然本公司會定期與特定客戶簽訂期貨/遠期合約，以經濟方式對抗某些原物料價格上漲的風險，但本公司可能無法有效應對這些原物料的價格波動。

天然氣是本公司大多數化學產品生產的主要原物料。雖然本公司與部分客戶簽訂合約，允許將原物料成本轉嫁給客戶，但本公司有相當多的銷售並未包含此類轉嫁條款。此外，本公司農產品的現貨銷售價格可能與天然氣成本無關，而是反映類似或競爭性氮源的市場條件。這種無關聯性可能影響本公司在該市場恢復全部生產成本的能力。因此，未來本公司可能無法將所有原物料成本的增加轉嫁給所有客戶。未來原物料價格波動可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運成果產生不利影響。
此外，本公司依賴某些供應商提供天然氣及其他製造產品所需的關鍵零組件。若天然氣及其他關鍵零組件供應中斷，可能導致生產中斷或出貨延遲。
北美地區天然氣價格波動性高，受地緣政治不穩定、國內鑽探活動程度及嚴重天氣事件造成的暫時供應中斷影響。此外，未來天然氣從頁巖層的生產可能因規範變更而減少，例如限制鑽探或水力壓裂、提高成本，或因油價下跌而減少石油勘探與開發，進而減少伴生天然氣的生產。此外，因工業需求增加、電力發電需求增加（特別是來自人工智慧資料中心）及天然氣出口增加，導致美國墨西哥灣沿岸地區天然氣需求增加，可能導致天然氣價格上漲。
本公司曾因天然氣及其他關鍵零組件成本過高或無法取得而暫停化學廠的生產，未來也可能因相同原因而暫停生產，這可能影響本公司在所服務市場的競爭力。因此，未來本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性及營運成果可能因天然氣及其他關鍵零組件無法取得，以及購買天然氣及其他關鍵零組件的成本增加而受到重大影響。

本公司在四個廠區製造產品。營運中斷可能因多種原因發生，包括天然災害、天氣、未預期的維護、其他製造問題、疾病、罷工或其他勞工不滿、運輸中斷等。極端天氣事件，包括溫度極端，根據嚴重程度與地點，不僅可能損害本公司廠區與中斷營運，也可能對本公司產品的配送產生不利影響。此外，本公司廠區可能因設備故障而無法運作，而這些設備可能難以更換或交貨時間極長，部分原因在於供應商數量有限，進而導致營運中斷。任何廠區的營運中斷，或因供應鏈中斷對任何廠區營運造成重大影響，可能影響本公司生產產品與履行承諾的能力，並對本公司流動性、財務狀況、營運成果與業務產生重大不利影響。
